translation.english_text: O image of beauty in whom all the world's loveliness has gathered—the fool came begging for love, and when you cried out, he kicked it aside and left. Dear Rani, do not be troubled. Your youth cannot be equalled even by the price of all fourteen worlds; your radiance cannot be found even on celestial women. I will not allow all this to be wasted in the storm called widowhood. Golden image won through penance, I am here to bow at your silken feet. Not only if you are a young widow—even if you had obtained a divorce today and come here straight from the court, I would still be ready to accept you.

translation.english_text: Babu! Stop babbling. Whether he pushes me away or embraces me, this heart has room only for my Raja. Rani belongs only to Raja. If he rejects that bond, Rani would sever her bond with the world itself rather than become a moth that falls into a flame like you.
Hmm. What would you do if Raja had never been born?
Why imagine that? Do now whatever you would have done if I myself had never been born.
Hmm. Rani belongs only to Raja. Rani belongs only to Raja. But if, with the trump card I play, that Raja himself gets cut down... hmm!
notes: The source's card-game metaphor is retained rather than expanded into an inferred plot action.
